notes.title: Update Inbound
notes.notes:
[p]For three hundred days, Jax Calder endured the hellscape of Bromius III, a wet barren rock scoured by wind and acid rain, where rusted metal groaned like ghosts and the sky never broke from its ashen shroud. Alone among the skeletons of the mining colony, he survived on emergency rations and grim determination, his only companion a failing environmental suit and the dim hum of a battered terminal he’d dragged into shelter piece by piece. Day after day, he worked—rebuilding the antenna from scrap, coding blind into cracked screens, shielding circuits with his body during electrical storms—until his hands bled and his breath stank of recycled air. 

Sleep came in fits but he was trained for this. And on the three-hundredth day, the terminal lit green. A signal broke through. And just before the storm season returned, a dark shape pierced the clouds—sleek, and familiar.  Just in time for Summer on Earth..
--
What some of you might remember is that AO was originally a game called [url="https://www.indiedb.com/games/zoo-base/news/aiming-for-misadventure-the-story-behind-zoo-base"]Zoo Base[/url]. And that Zoo Base was inspired by Star Zoo by Bay12. Fun fact - it wasn’t just inspired by it but we even got permission to directly call it a spiritual sequel.[/p][p]
Then everything got entirely too overthought. In an attempt to distinguish AO from predecessor Zoo Base. In hindsight that was a bad idea.[/p][p]
Which is not to say that I regret doing that. It’s just that with the state of the industry being what it is, there is a new kind of clarity hitting a lot of folks who have been indie for far longer than expected.[/p][p]
I think a lot of us are coming back to thinking about what fun is. Since like the tech industry as a whole there was a lot of problem solving of things that didn’t really need fixing. A lot of reintroductions to the wheel. And while the results are still valuable, I think a lot of engineers are figuring out how to apply those lessons and new technologies in a way that isn’t so heavily R&D.
[/p][p]Right now the server is (still) down in preparation for V7 - expected before July - which should put AO on a clear track to be exiting early access within a few subsequent patches. The game itself is being simplified because it actually outgrew itself around the time of the Linux announcement.  Which itself was marred with issues and quietly delayed and unknown outside of Discord.

More on all that in the next one! 

[/p]

notes.title: Apsis Online NPC Story Engine Update
notes.notes:
The shanty-town outside the walls of Bromius Central at night is awash in shadows against firelit panels of rusted sheet metal.  Old hull parts dot the overgrowth and makeshift awnings while several human children in ragged tunics gather around a large murky puddle. All laughing and splashing beneath bare feet. A two-headed human brushes against your right shoulder with a glare from the face close enough to make out. His bluish bloated lips scowling with stringy chin-length dark hair flipped aside revealing scars along his cheek.  

The other head droops, remaining flailing helplessly at his side as he hurries away toward the city gate. Carrying a large metal container on his back secured by worn leather straps. Moon and firelight unsteadily reveal the faded letters “HGEC” as you determine that he may have been in the parts and organ trade. Here in the clone camps you can’t be too sure anyway. This is where anyone can end up after all. One way or another.

–
In the upcoming Apsis Online v7 I will be introducing a new simulation engine. Which is meant to activate the living game world starting with its first inhabitants (human or otherwise) and continuing through to their descendants and the resulting economic conditions that will effect the initial colony in more visible and impactful ways.

[img]https://cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/1552260/ss_ce4ed6b05c435c7d173448da0535addb189b2f54.600x338.jpg?t=1696530880[/img]

Each NPC will also have their own story generated for them and at some point I will be making those accessible via their communications screen. This could be helpful in determining their underlying motives and potential skills. As well as compatibility with other NPC you may need to bring them around. A retired UESA soldier who is now a clone might not enjoy being asked to work with a Mutroon or Vane raider for example. Think [i]Football Manager[/i] in space.

This means that the player (you) will no longer be limited to small interactions with preset NPCs. The goal is to make you feel like an inhabitant of an existing place that you can impact with you decisions.  If you are familiar with the current NPC system you may have noticed a lot of speech options. The initial purpose of this was to test out their dynamic outlook on static game worlds down to things like recognizing the player, their faction and to some extent the choices they’ve already made.

Scaling this system means making the world feel very persistent. Which when coupled with more activities and embark options will allow anyone to effect everyone. Current plans include land and orbital patrols coupled with special tasks issued by NPCs. A lot like how adventure mode in DF Classic operates when looking for things to do.

So the overworld is returning as a real-time map allowing you to get information of zones as well as take specific actions in them for reasons that will also see expansions over the next few builds. NPCs will now settle scouted areas and can be raided. Players interrupting herds will effect the local economy. Air and land patrols will earn you experience and clout with the UESA which can unlock governance options when promoted. And dying may see you cloned and respawned in a clone camp where players can buy and sell grey market items like body parts, animals/people or simply hire personnel.

I may be jumping the gun on this post as we are still at least days away from a release but I felt it was important to do a little tell. In other news we’re still running on old servers but some optimization has made this bearable enough. A new server does exists but I'd hate to migrate then migrate back. The next patch will also include general stability and “quality of life” updates. More info coming soon. And thanks for your patience!

notes.title: Apsis Online V7 Update+
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39863067/b54ca1c06ac91367beca83592168a547c941d172.gif[/img]

Today is Waveday on the 15th of Rimmoon. The air is heavy with humidity.  I can feel the ground beneath as lush and damp as always.  Everywhere, the sound of water trickling and cascading is ever-present. Lightning illuminated a sheet of dark clouds pulled across the sky and, at times, this planet would be caught in a seemingly eternal rainfall.

The rain would become puddles and lakes but that is when you can see the Nutroon (`n) eggs float up toward the surface, waiting to hatch..

***

It is these creatures that will be the focus of V7 . As well as their less benign counterparts the Mutroon (`m). This update will coincide with a Steam launch. 

Today I was able to talk to our server sponsor to get test builds live again. So that means the most current build of the game is already up for internal testing.

Some other changes to expect by V7:

[+] Factions V1 will allow players to issue referrals to friends for mutual perks.
[+] Combat V2 is nothing at all like combat V1 and a departure from the traditional roguelike formula.
[+] Real-time data.
[+] Expanded NPC AI
[+] Expanded player profiles + player stories (auto-updated web pages).
[+] Bases (special points of interest on a planet, allows missions)
[+] Exploration V1

[b]Delayed features[/b]

Genetic engineering (I know)

For more upcoming information check out the Discord: https://discord.gg/m8KCv4j
